Overview / Features / Companion Field App
The team’s side of the incident

The assignment in hand. The field in the picture.

The ArcHorizon companion app gives assigned personnel the details they need to work, a map for context, and a fast way to report status and findings. Updates return to the same incident record used by command and planning.

Explore the field screen ↓How updates move →
The working screen

Start with the assignment, then stay with the narrative.

The home view centers the team’s current assignment. A compact header shows task details and a single free-text location field; the narrative feed gives the team a running account of what has happened.

At the topCurrent task, team context, and location.
In the centerAssignment and narrative updates in the order the team needs them.
Within reachStatus controls followed by actions for intel, narrative, messaging, and hazards.
Know the work

Task details and map context travel together.

A team can open the full assignment for objectives, timing, supervisor, hazards, and additional instructions. The map keeps the assigned area, access, and related features close to that description.

Task detail

The fuller task record is available when the short home summary is not enough.

Map

Geometry and operational features carry through from the desktop planning and GIS workspaces.

How Operations creates an assignment →How GIS supplies the geography →
Status and check-in

Update the team’s position in the operation.

Status controls are available on the working screen, so the team can report movement and availability without leaving the assignment. Check-in and status are reflected in Operations.

Briefed / en routeThe team has its instructions and is moving toward the work.
Arrived / workingOperations can see that the team reached its area and started the task.
Returning / availableThe resource comes back into the picture for debriefing or reassignment.

Team status describes the resource. Task status describes progress on the assignment. Both remain visible to staff.

Field reporting

Capture the detail while it is still fresh.

The app places reporting actions after the live narrative so a team can document an observation at the point of work and keep the context attached to its task. Focused sheets or dialogs let the team submit a report and return to the working screen.

01 / NARRATIVE

Record the sequence

Add a tasking, safety, critical, or general entry to the incident narrative. The category helps readers find the type of update without adding a significance scale.

02 / INTEL

Send a finding

Report a clue or observation with its location and context for intelligence review and possible follow-up.

03 / HAZARDS

Flag a condition

Identify a hazard that affects the team or the next assignment, and carry its location into the operational picture.

04 / MESSAGING

Coordinate directly

Exchange assignment-related information with the people coordinating the work.

One record across devices

What the team sends changes what staff can see.

The field app is a focused part of ArcHorizon. It uses the task and map prepared on desktop, then returns status and observations to the modules that need them.

OperationsAssigns the team and receives check-in, status, and task progress.
IntelligenceReceives clues and observations for review, leads, and follow-up.
Safety & GISSee hazards in the assignment and on the map.
Incident recordRetains the narrative and activity that support reports and debriefings.
Command & planningUse the changing picture to adjust priorities and the next assignment.
More than one operating context

Search response and planned events use the same foundation.

The companion app adapts the field view to the incident type. A search team needs its area and task details; a planned event team may need schedule and position information in the same assignment framework.

  • Show the details that matter to the current event or response.
  • Keep team status and field narrative in the shared record.
  • Use the same desktop coordination path for both types of work.
Field hardware

Room to work on a tablet.

The landscape tablet view uses the additional space for an MDT-style layout: assignment, narrative, map, and actions can be read together without turning the field screen into a desktop command console.

Focused access

Give each person the right view.

Field users work primarily within their team assignment. Incident members have the write actions needed for that role; external participants can be given a view-only picture. The desktop retains the broader command and administrative tools.
